notes.title: Patch 0.27.0
notes.content:
[b]Halloween Event: Zombie Apocalypse![/b]

Be the last survivor remaining or the Top Zombie to earn the most Credits and Valor in each round!
- Eliminate all the other players to become the Winner of the round!
- Credits are used to purchase skins and Valor contributes to your Rank, which allows you to have more Nobles and population.
- Players start off with 4 Villagers and the Pack Horse with resources on a random island.
- Stone, Tin, Copper and Iron lodes randomly spawn on the map while Trees and Farms can be built.

[b]Technological Advance[/b]
The Bandit, Zombie and Knight Boss quests allow you to access better metals and equipment like the Matchlock.
But are you able to defeat them without being ambushed by the other players?
With great risks comes great rewards!

Last Safe Haven
After 1 hour, the Zombie Apocalypse will begin. The zombies will periodically take over Castles that are furthest away from a secretly chosen Castle that will be the humans' final stand.

[b]Become the Top Zombie[/b]
Being reborn as a Zombie isn't the end, but a new beginning. They have special powers:
1. A higher jump that allows you to land on a block.
2. Occasional wolf howl that reveals the positions of the humans.
3. Increasing strength over time.
4. Zombies' strength increases when a human player is eliminated by a Zombie.
5. Also command a small gang of zombies!

[b]Changes:[/b]
- Support for private servers is disabled. All players are automatically connected to our new Linux public server based in North America.
- Assign Villagers to work and sleep at a Castle from a dropdown menu instead of through the dialogue.
- F6-F10 commands are changed with addition of: Only nearby villagers to heal, and Only villagers below 50% to heal.
- Mounting and dismounting horse commands shifted to the Escape Menu.
- Villagers with melee weapons will only charge forward if the enemy is within 15 meters.
- As an experiment, Castles will remain instead of being wiped in even Rounds.

notes.title: Patch 0.26.0
notes.content:
[b]Education System and Skill Perks[/b]
- Enrol into courses by speaking to a Teacher at the Queenstown University on the Dreadnaught Cliffs!
- Starting with Literacy for Dummies, buy the skill books from a Merchant.
- Your Academy must have Teacher Tables and Student Desks assigned to them (like in a classroom setting).
- Your Library must have Bookshelves with the skill books inside.
- Students will study during their leisure time and when the course has advanced to the next day.
- They will go to the Library to take their books and study.
- Study progress and study actions can be found in the People panel under the Studies tab.
- To start studying, select the desired action in the Studies tab.

- A course spans over 4 in-game days:
Day 1: Read your textbook in hand wherever you wish.
Day 2: Attend the lecture at your chosen Academy.
Day 3: Do homework with your textbook in hand and be seated wherever you wish.
Day 4: Sit for the examination at your chosen Academy.

- Graduating from a course promotes the skill to the next level if you achieve a passing grade of E and above.
- Getting a good grade increases the experience boost for the skill.
- Attaining higher skill ranks make you a lot more proficient at your skill perks.
- Details of these skill perks can be found in the description of the skill books.
- [b]Coming soon:[/b] Writing better skill books at Scholar's Desks and having villagers working as Teachers and Scholars.

[b]Changes:[/b]
- Dangerous Lands rewards reduced appropriately as they were breaking the economy.
- Engineers earn similarly to Bartenders instead of a flat 5,000 (Strength multiplied by skill rank and 10,000).
- Skills sorted by level and rank in descending order.

notes.title: Patch 0.25.0
notes.content:
[b]Inventory System Revamp[/b]

- If the items in your belt aren't updating properly, you can press U to reload from the server.
- Items in the inventory window can be dragged and dropped around.
- Items can hold up to 9 quintillion in quantity as it has been upgraded from 32 to 64-bit integers.
- Added Stash buttons beside the Loot ones in the inventory window, which functions the opposite of Loot.
- Client and server transactions sends and receives acknowledgment to each other, up to 3 attempts if they fail.

[b]Changes:[/b]
- Added Sayo's first female hairstyle! A big thanks to @Sayo! 😄 
- Mutual wars are allowed during enforced rule.
- Villagers spawn around the Town Bell when summoned and try to get into formation.
- Mob kills by nobles no longer give crowns.
- Dangerous Lands quests give crowns per mob kill upon quest completion: 400 each for Easy, 600 for Normal, 800 for Hard and 1000 for Nosajimiki.
- Princes/Princesses can also build settlements.
- Added [No Specific Plot] option when assigning villagers' workplaces or hometowns.
- Offline ceasefire duration increased from 10 to 30 minutes.

notes.title: Patch 0.24.0
notes.content:
[b]Work and Lifestyle Schedules[/b]
- One in-game day consists of 12 segments of 5 minutes each (1 hour in total).
- Added Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner segments, where villagers will automatically have their meals.
- Added the Bedtime segment, where villagers will sleep around 1-2 minutes.
- Villagers will automatically fulfill their needs throughout the day.
- Villagers will only work between Dawn to Dusk. When it's Early Evening onwards, they will not work and continuously do activities like dancing, playing instrument and praying.
- Guards are an exception, they will not fulfill any needs until you relieve them from their duty, and only go to sleep when their HP is below 40%.

[b]Changes:[/b]
- Added a stables in Caringtown.
- Needs deplete at different speeds, with Call of Nature being the fastest.
- Dancing and playing instrument fills up the Fun meter.

[b]Fixes:[/b]
- Valor resetting to 0 after killing mobs/working at goldsmith desks.
- Horses not showing its name and owner above their heads.
- Kingdom leaders being demoted to Prince/Princesses.

notes.title: Patch 0.23.0
notes.content:
[b]Forge the Crown to become the Emperor of the Realm![/b]
- Work at a Goldsmith's Desk to add progress towards the completion of the Crown.
- They can be built in Castles/Siege Camps, found under Work Furniture.
- Each Goldsmith will add 1 Crown point every 30 seconds.
- Only Kings/Queens can gain crown progress and can only contribute to his/her own crown progress.
- Goldsmiths do not earn any income, but a big and juicy reward of [b]2 billion gold coins[/b] when you're the first to forge the Crown.
- Upon completion, you'll gain the Emperor title and the entire realm will be reunited under your banner for one whole week.

[b]Phase 1 - Race to complete the forging of the Crown [/b]
- In this phase, PvP players should/would want to hinder each other's crown progresses so that they can clinch the huge reward and the benefits of becoming Emperor.
- Crown progresses will be shown in the Diplomacy panel so that you can view each other's progress.
- A Crown leaderboard will show the top three players with the highest crown progresses.
- The first to reach 100% will obtain the reward and gain the title of Emperor and rule over the entire realm.
- Only one player can become the Emperor, every other kingdom will be disbanded and everyone will automatically join the Emperor's Kingdom.
- Everyone's banners and colors will follow the Emperor's.

[b]Phase 2 - Era of Stability, Peace and Taxes to the Emperor[/b]
- The Emperor will have a complete enforced rule of the realm for 1 week from the moment he made the Crown.
- Other players will have their King/Queen title downgraded to Prince/Princess, and no one else can form another Kingdom.
- The settlements will still belong to the respective players and they can still build in it, but they won't be able to settle new towns as they cannot be King/Queen.
- Other players will not be able to leave his Kingdom until the enforced rule is over.
- Everyone will have their Crown progress reset to 0 and cannot gain any progress, until the enforced rule is over.
- Everyone else will start paying 20% of their income in taxes to the Emperor.

[b]Phase 3 - The Fall of the Empire[/b]
- Once the enforce rule ends, other players can choose to leave his Kingdom and break free to form their own Kingdoms and banner colors again.
- The cycle will restart back to Phase 1 only when the current Emperor is killed, he would lose his Emperor title and everyone can start making progress in their Crowns again.

[b]Added 4 Skills, 5 Jobs, 5 Needs[/b]

- The 5 new jobs can be found under working "At an indoors job as..." choice.
- Currently, there's no penalties for having 0 or low amounts in the needs.
- Animations for all needs are currently placeholders, proper ones will be added soon.

Dancing -  Dance by pressing L. Experience is gained only when you complete a dance, so spamming will not gain anything.
Logic -  Gain experience in Logic by sitting at a chess table, which also fills up your Fun needs.
Faith -  Gain experience in Faith by praying at an altar, which also fills up your Faith needs. Note: A workbench is the current placeholder, until the model comes in.
Playing Instrument -  Play an instrument by pressing K. Experience is gained after 10 seconds. Note: A shield is the current placeholder, until an instrument model comes in. Proper animations and local music will be added soon.

Bard -  Requires a Bar. Recommended to have a 3x3 flat area in front of the Bar. Trains the Playing Instrument skill. All the Bards can use the same Bar.
Bartender -  Requires a Bar. Trains the Commerce skill. Only one Bartender per Bar. Functions very similarly to Treasurers. They will have functionalities added in the future.
Chess Player -  Requires a Chess Table. Recommended to have a 3x3 flat area in front of the Bar. Trains the Logic skill. Up to two Chess Players per table.
Dancer -  Requires a Bar. Recommended to have a 3x3 flat area in front of the Bar. Trains the Dancing skill. All the Dancers can use the same Bar. 
Monk -  Requires an Altar. Recommended to have a 3x3 flat area in front of the Altar. Trains the Faith skill.  All the Monks can use the same Altar.

Thirst -  Regain Thirst by sitting at a Bar. Recovers at a relatively quick rate.
Fun -  Regain Fun by sitting at a Chess Table. Takes a little while to recover.
Call of Nature -  Regain Call of Nature by sitting at a toilet. Recovers at the fastest rate.
Cleanliness -  Regain Cleanliness by sitting at a toilet. Recovers at a relatively quick rate.
Faith -  Regain Faith by praying at an Altar. Takes a little while to recover.

- Weapons and tools sell prices reduced from 50% to 30% and metal bars sell prices reduced from 30% to 20%.
- Seats no longer regain health and energy.

[b]Rental[/b]

Plot Size: 51x51x15

Plot Size: 51x51x10
You can build all the resources and Rental Plots.
Can be built up to 20 blocks away from non-allied settlements.

Plot Size: 27x27x10

notes.title: Patch 0.20.0
notes.content:
[b]Tutorial Quest Revamp[/b]
- Added 3 starting tutorial Story quests that should help new players familiarize better to the game.

[b]Changes:[/b]
- Movement speed reduced from 600 to 400 for sprinting, walking/combat speed reduced from 300 to 200, for a more realistic feel.
- Villagers walk instead of running for most tasks, while still running when following or going to bed.
- All purchased maximum population will be reset to 0 upon death.

notes.title: Patch 0.19.0
notes.content:
[b]Social Interactions, Charm skill and Nobility[/b]
- Voice audio for the dialogues will be added in the next patch.
- You can now receive Introductions when talking to your villager for the first time, and initiate conversations that will either increase/decrease your friendship/relationship.
- It's basically a guessing and memory minigame, which a short random conversation will be picked from a small pool and each villager will have their own sets of answers.
- Choosing the correct/wrong choice will add 5 or -3 to the friendship/relationship and give 50 or 30 exp to both the villager's and your Charm skill respectively.
- Every level in Charm gives you stats and a 0.3% chance of succeeding a failed conversation.
- You can only have one conversation per villager for each in-game day (1 real-life hour).
- Villagers will also introduce themselves to each other, and have conversations within 10m with other villagers throughout the day.
- They won't have a conversation with other villagers who are engaged in combat or dialogue.
- Reaching 50 Friendship will unlock the Start a Friendly Banter choice, with another pool of dialogues.
- Reaching 100 Friendship will unlock Initiate a Romantic Conversation, gaining points will increase your Relationship.
- Having a good relationship score will bring benefits in the future.
- It also unlocks the ability to appoint your close friend as a Noble, if you are at least an Emperor/Empress. 

[b]Nobles[/b]
- The hardcore rouge-like gameplay aspect of permadeath has been re-added, due to the polls being in favor and as it aligns better with the direction of future features.
- Non-nobles will perma-die and get killed when reaching 0 HP, while Nobles will be captured as prisoners instead.
- You can have up to (Maximum population divided by 10) Nobles in your realm.
- Nobles will gain a lot more functionality in the future.

[b]Changes:[/b]
- Experience gain from mining ores has been tripled, and smelting bars has been doubled.
- Desk/Seat jobs now also gain Level experience.
- Melee attacks can now detect walls and blocks and convert them into damageable ones, instead of a single line trace in front of your character.
- Gunshots can now convert walls/blocks too.

- Villagers having the same name causing issues. New villagers should not have the same name as any of the current villagers.

notes.title: Patch 0.17 - Non-building Gameplay and Ransom Prisoners
notes.content:
[h2]Non-building Gameplay and Ransom Prisoners[/h2]
- Every player and their villagers are now free to use all the facilities that are available in any town, while using their pack horse as a portable stockpile.
- This feature caters to non-building players who would like to play as a wandering merchant / mercenary band, without the need to construct anything at all.
- Bed assignment UI is available to all players regardless of town ownership.
- Villagers will no longer be arriving for free as a family, you have to hire them from any town, with a limited caravan quantity that replenishes when the current merchant goes back to Caringtown and a new merchant arrives.
- The hardcore rouge-like gameplay aspect of the game has been removed, as we feel that dropping all loot, losing all valor and rank is punishing enough. We hope that this will encourage more PvP as a lot lesser progress would be at stake in a war.
- Players and villagers no longer permanently die upon reaching zero HP. Instead, only the loot, valor and rank of a player is lost, while a villager will become a prisoner.
- To get back your villagers, simply talk to any merchant and select the Ransom a villager option. Every level incurs a 1000 gold cost.
- Villagers captured by enemy players in a PvP war will be at the mercy of the victor, he/she can choose to let them go for free, or negotiate with the other party. A timer will be imposed soon, so that they won't be prisoners forever.

[h2]Changes:[/h2]
- The 90% protection for players Squire and below have been removed, due to the removal of permadeath.
- Shield damage reduction have been reduced from 60% to 40%, as shield-bearers were becoming very difficult to deal with.
- UI of the number of beds have been separated from current and max population.

notes.title: Patch 0.15 - Governor of the Islands
notes.content:
[h2]Governor of the Islands:[/h2]
- The Prince/Princess or ranks above that is online with the highest valor (previously known as honor) and castle on an island will become the governor of that island. If that player goes offline, the next in-line will become the governor. If there's no online Princes/Princesses or higher on that island, then nobody will be ruling that island.
- A tax rate with a minimum of 2 million and a maximum of 10 million has to be paid to the governor. The taxes are deducted when your villagers get their wages. Make sure to leave enough gold in the stockpile. Else, villagers will stop working, and the island governor will not be happy.

Changes:
- Increased rank requirements by 10 times, so that newcomers don't reach the maximum rank too quickly.
- Increased amount of Valor purchased, from 100 to 1000 and balanced the cost per purchase.
